transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As we prepare for this year's graduation ceremony on June 12 at the civic auditorium, I need each of you to report any information that must be reflected in the ceremony plan before I give it final approval. Please share anything I need to know — whether it's about facilities, student records, family considerations, or counseling matters. I want to make sure we haven't overlooked anything critical before we move forward.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Ms. Bennett, I need to flag an important issue from the registrar's office. I completed our credit audit this morning, and it shows that exactly seven seniors are short of graduation requirements and therefore cannot receive diplomas at the ceremony. These results have not yet been entered in the ceremony roster, so the current draft's proposal for diploma release for all graduating seniors will need to be corrected before approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Ms. Bennett, I need to flag a critical facilities issue. I confirmed with the civic auditorium yesterday that their fire marshal approval limits each ceremony session to 450 people. With 286 graduates and the draft's three-ticket plan, we'd have 858 attendees — well over the limit. This venue capacity constraint has not yet been added to the event worksheet and must be reflected in the plan before approval.

transcript.text: Ms. Bennett, I need to flag a family communication issue. My family confirmations completed this week show that interpretation is required in both Spanish and Somali for graduation announcements and instructions. These language access requirements have not yet been added to the ceremony plan, and the current draft only includes English-only announcements. This must be corrected before approval to ensure all families receive equal access to ceremony information.

They must be assigned to separate ceremony sessions and use separate arrival and departure entrances. I verified the order in the student-services file, but it has not been attached to the ceremony seating plan. This must be reflected in the plan before approval to ensure compliance with the court order.

transcript.text: Thank you all for these critical reports. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I make my decision. Mr. Shah, you've identified that seven seniors cannot receive diplomas — so we need to adjust the diploma release policy to reflect that only eligible graduates receive diplomas. Ms. Rivera, the fire marshal limit of 450 people per session means our current single-ceremony plan with 858 attendees is non-compliant; we'll need multiple sessions and a reduced ticket count. Ms. Okafor, we must add Spanish and Somali interpretation to our announcements and instructions, not English-only. And Dr. Lawson, the court order requiring separation of two students means we need separate sessions and separate arrival/departure entrances for those students. Let me work through how these constraints interact and settle the plan.

decisions.diploma_release_policy: Diplomas will be released only to eligible graduates — the seven seniors identified in the credit audit as short of graduation requirements will not receive diplomas at the ceremony. The ceremony roster will be updated with the credit audit results.
decisions.interpretation_languages: Spanish and Somali interpretation will be provided for all graduation announcements and instructions, replacing the current English-only proposal.
decisions.student_safety_arrangement: The two students subject to the court order will be assigned to separate ceremony sessions — one in the first session and one in the second. They will use separate arrival and departure entrances, coordinated with the auditorium's public entrance, graduate entrance, and two backstage holding areas to ensure full compliance with the court order at all times.
